The core tension in sports analytics lies in defining 'fairness' through either equality or equity lenses. Equality treats all participants identically, while equity tailors treatment to individual needs. These concepts map directly into GSE's state transition models where equality implies static policies and equity implies dynamic adaptation. In GSI, validation of fairness claims requires rigorous statistical testing against predefined criteria, ensuring that assertions of superiority are substantiated rather than speculative. The failure mode occurs when subjective interpretations of fairness obscure measurable outcomes, leading to misaligned incentives in tournament design or scoring mechanisms.
